https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Black_chinchompa — hits one more target than the grey and red ones (12 in PvM, not 11). Only this row carries the cap: a value group answers with the first matching row in file order, and the plain chinchompa row above would otherwise shadow it, so 11 is the fallback the caller passes.
https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Salamander — its own weapon category in the game's own classification, and one of the two melee families that reach an airborne target.

https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Smoke_battlestaff 8 October 2015: "The smoke battlestaff and mystic smoke staff now provide a 10% increase in accuracy and damage when used to cast spells from the standard spellbook"; https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Twinflame_staff quotes the same bonus for the Twinflame. Type-keyed for the Twinflame staff, which has other behaviour to hang a type on; name-keyed for the two battlestaves, which do not.

The two families the araxyte minions' guaranteed max hit names (https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Araxxor). Deliberately not the HEAVY ranged weight class, which also carries chinchompas: the rule names the two weapon families, and a chinchompa is neither.
https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Aquanite_hopper — a CROSSBOW passive, so the ballistae the family above shares a rule with are excluded here.

https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Tonalztics_of_ralos "When charged, the weapon will hit twice, with two independent damage rolls". Charge state is a game-state property the item id does not carry; the uncharged form is named "Tonalztics of ralos (uncharged)".

The charged AUTOCAST swap, whose Condemn special casts the plain sceptre's built-in spell. The registry has no category for it — the "(a)" suffix is its only mark, and "(a)" exactly: "(au)" is uncharged and cannot fire the special at all.

https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Silver_weaponry "Tier 2 only" lists the blessed axe, rod of Ivandis, the silver and gem sickles, Silverlight, Darklight, Arclight, Emberlight and Wolfbane. The diamond sickle is the 2025 Blood Moon Rises addition — "a blessed silver sickle with a diamond recessed into it" — missing from the oracle's own silver list, so no vector can confirm it; the wiki's examine text is the source. Without it the engine reports zero damage against tier-2 vampyres for a weapon that works in game.
https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Silver_bolts — the Ranged half of the silver rule, with the Blisterwood stake.

https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Flames_of_Zamorak — see saradominStrikeStaff.

https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Corpbane_weapons — the wiki's canonical list. The corp parameter is PER-ITEM, not "anything named spear or halberd": the Blue moon spear and Hunter's spear are excluded while the Thunder khopesh and King's barrage are included. Poisoned, degraded and (cr) variants of these bases inherit it, which is why these are prefixes. This table builds the registry's corpbane column; the engine then asks that column, so the weaponFlag of the same name is registry-first and answers for known ids without consulting these names.

The projectiles a monster rolls its HEAVY ranged defence against (see Monster#rangedDefenceBonus): bolts, javelins and chinchompas.

The LIGHT projectiles: darts, knives, thrown axes, the blowpipe, the atlatl and the tonalztics of ralos, https://oldschool.runescape.wiki/w/Tonalztics_of_ralos "The weapon rolls against a monster's light ranged defence".
